reason: The first reading's 'Melcherus' (15 Jan.) is Wernherus, '4 Non' (168-11r) is 4 Idus (10 Feb.), and the names Sanegans, Rubeiner, Krappel, Leibolvingen and Werthaim were completed from the edition where the strips are worn or cut.
sources: MGH, Necrologia Germaniae III: Dioeceses Brixinensis, Frisingensis, Ratisbonensis, ed. S. Herzberg-Fränkel (Berlin 1905), Necrologium Stamsense pp. 47-59 (preface p. 47; 9-15 Jan. p. 48; 9-13 Feb. p. 49; 24 Feb. p. 50), archive.org monumentagenecro03geseuoft pages n60-n63
P. M. Grebenc, typed slips and envelope (1964-1965), photographed on the record, canvases 5 and 8-15
text:
F-tnqw (Stams, STA, Frg. 168) - source-assisted reading. Read with the MGH Necrologia III text (pp. 48-50) and the archivist's typed slips available. A research reader reread on the image, from contrast-enhanced native crops: 168-1r 13-15 January; 168-11r whole face; 168-11v whole face; 168-7v top lines. 168-11v was also read by a second reader before the edition was consulted. 168-1v and the other items rest on the image-only first reading. Expansions in (), uncertain readings ?, losses [...]. Readings inside [] that name a word (e.g. [Kirchperg]) are not on the strip.
